usual_baseline: Positioning standards are often missed. Calibration marker balls were present in 44–45% [1322, 1708]. Lateral ankle talar domes superimposed in 61% [1705]; wrist piso-scapho-capitate relationship 50% [1726]. 69/100 arthroplasty films were adequate [1619]. Only 23.09% of shoulder AP views met criteria and 21.17% had an axillary view [1653].
fix_that_works: Posters plus teaching by an associate specialist raised talar dome superimposition from 61% to 85% [1705] and wrist relationship from 50% to 82% [1726]. Posters, a radiographer presentation and a mandatory checklist raised marker ball presence from 45% to 78% [1708]. A protocol and ordering rota raised timely templating films from 20% to 70% [1681]. Guidelines and feedback raised adequate arthroplasty films from 69/100 to 84/100 [1619].
fix_that_fails: Calibration marker compliance fell to 44% after an earlier improvement from 64% to 73% [1322]. Pubic symphysis centring reached only 47% and GT/LT level 43% [1619]. Overall marker compliance change was not significant (59% to 80%, p=0.132) [1708].
consultant_advice: Radiograph positioning audits improve quickly with posters and joint teaching of radiographers and doctors, but gains fade [1322]. Involve the radiography team from the start and build checks into the request or checklist. More useful is measuring whether poor films led to repeat exposure or missed injury, which none of these assessed.
